title: Volunteers for the Fatal Wedding of Martyrdom

blocks.text: The congregation answers Gurbakhsh Singh's challenge by recognizing both his resolve and the gravity of the moment. He asks who would accompany him on this fatal wedding expedition, and the image of martyrdom as a wedding with death turns the coming battle into a consciously embraced offering rather than a desperate last stand.

The Singhs respond immediately. Many a Singh volunteered, bowing at his feet and declaring that they too were ready to give their heads, for by sacrificing their lives would they be wedding death in the Guru's cause and making good on the ideals taught in the Panth.

The page also frames their zeal within scriptural and historical memory. Such a description has been given in Chandi Astotar, and as news spreads that the Singhs had assembled at Amritsar, the contrast sharpens between those inspired to heroic sacrifice and those whose weaker hearts begin to flee from Abdali's advance.
